title: Bunk living with the Lofburrs and Freddie Moore, and the padlocked telephone
summary: Bunk's New York residences, the padlock on Freddie Moore's wife's telephone, and Bunk idle and ignored in New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, he was living with the Lofburrs, as I recall, most of the time. There was also a period when he was living with... Who was it? Kaiser Marshall? Yeah. Kaiser Marshall's apartment, was it? No. No. The other drummer. Not Kaiser.
Freddie Moore. Freddie Moore's apartment. That's right.
That's the time that his wife put the... Freddie Moore's wife...
Put the padlock on the telephone, yeah. Yeah. Bunk was very offended. And I used to...
Did he tell you then? That he said...

Yeah, yeah. He told me... He said he couldn't understand why people acted like that. That all he had to do was just tell him not to use the phone, and he wouldn't use the phone. But here he was sitting in his easy chair, and the phone was right at his elbow, and this was his spot in the apartment, and there was a constant reminder that he kind of wasn't welcome, I guess, or that there was a limited welcome. Yeah. Yeah. So, but he invited me, you know, up to spend the afternoons with him. I guess this was a period when there was absolutely nothing going on, and New York has a way of forgetting about you as fast as it can get excited about you. And so at this particular time, Bunk had absolutely nothing happening, and he was just... I would go up wherever he was staying, and just find him, and it's kind of dozing off in an easy chair, looking out of the window. He almost never had any visitors, you know, during that time. Nobody even cared to go up and talk to him. Probably didn't even know he was there, actually. Yeah, probably hasn't. He probably thought he was back in New Orleans. But, uh...
